_comment: Personal-copy template (schema version 2): one chapter of a published book that you own a copy of. Normally you do not write this by hand: save the book as a UTF-8 .txt and run npm run corpus:convert -- book.txt --lang th --work <slug> (docs/IMPORT.md, 'Your own copy of a book'). Copy this file only to see every field. Fields starting with an underscore are ignored by the validator.
title: Title of the book — Chapter 1

corpus.title: Your books
corpus._comment: One 'Your books' corpus per language: every personal copy goes here.

source.title: Title of the book
source.author: Author of the book
source.attribution: Title of the book — Author of the book. Your own copy; not distributed.
source.provenance: Supplied by the learner from a personal copy (my paperback, 12th printing); transcription not checked.
source._comment: rights 'personal-copy' + authorship 'published' + a provenance: the text is readable on this device without a review, labelled 'Your copy'. It is refused for Scripture ('Scripture is never a personal copy: it must be an identified, verified translation') and for generated text ('generated text is not a published work'). Personal copies are never bundled: keep the files under data/private/, not data/corpus/.

review._comment: No review is needed for a personal copy. Leave it 'unreviewed' until a person has checked your transcription against the book.

work._comment: Where this text sits in the course ladder: the slug of a work in src/course, and the chapter. courseId is optional (default: the first course for this language). Chapter 0 is front matter.

notes.body: Replace this with a short note of your own about the word or the sentence.
notes._comment: A document-level note belongs to the first sentence whose exact text contains 'match' (add "occurrence": 2 for the second such sentence). A note never changes the text. kind: cultural | regional | register | literary | historical | clause-structure. A note written by a person needs nothing more; a machine note ('provenance': 'machine') stays unreviewed until a named person reviews it ('reviewStatus' and 'by').

paragraphs._comment: One raw paragraph per line of the book, exactly as printed. Thai has no full stop: the importer finds the sentences. Do not add spaces.
paragraphs.text: ใส่ข้อความจากหนังสือของคุณที่นี่
